title: A memory store records what was true, not until when, so retrieval confidently returns a superseded fact
problem: The agent told me the deploy command, in detail and with confidence, and it was the command we replaced in April; the note it retrieved was written before the change and nothing in the store knows that.
symptom: An agent asserts an out-of-date fact about the project or the user, and the memory it cites is genuinely in the store: the retrieval was correct and the record was stale.
why_now: Agent memory was built as append-plus-embed because that is what retrieval needs, so writes carry text and tags but no validity interval and no supersession link. Retrieval then ranks by similarity, and a superseded record is exactly as similar to the query as its replacement, so it is preferentially returned when it happens to be worded better.
existing: Recency weighting in ranking: makes a stale record less likely to win, never unable to win, and it cannot tell a still-true old fact from a superseded one.
Periodic manual review of memory files: works, and is unbounded human labour that scales with the store rather than with the change rate.
Model-driven memory rewriting on conflict: needs the conflict to be noticed inside one context window, which is exactly what a long-horizon store does not guarantee.

evidence.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
evidence.quote: commercial chat assistants and long-context LLMs showing a 30% accuracy drop on memorizing information across sustained interactions
evidence.note: ICLR 2025. Its five measured abilities include knowledge updates and temporal reasoning, which is the academic name for this failure, and the measured drop is large.

evidence.title: How Claude remembers your project - Claude Code Docs
evidence.quote: if two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily
evidence.note: The vendor's own remedy for a superseded instruction is periodic human review to remove outdated or conflicting entries, which concedes there is no mechanism that retires one. Undated documentation page; the date is the retrieval date.

evidence.title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
evidence.quote: Even a single distractor reduces performance relative to the baseline (needle only), and adding four distractors compounds this degradation further.
evidence.note: A superseded memory is the strongest possible distractor because it is topically identical to the correct one, and this measures what one distractor costs. Undated technical report; the date is the retrieval date.

build_hypothesis: Two fields and one filter: every memory row carries a validity interval and an optional superseded_by link, a write that contradicts an existing row sets that link instead of appending beside it, and retrieval filters superseded rows before ranking rather than hoping recency outranks them.

check.manual_question: Your agent writes to a memory store. When a fact it remembered stops being true, what marks the old record so retrieval stops returning it, and what happens to rows written before that mechanism existed?
check.rationale: A store with writes and no supersession or validity vocabulary anywhere in its code cannot express that a record has stopped being true, so its retrieval path has nothing to filter on. It can be wrong in two ways: a project may model validity in a schema file or migration this pattern does not read, giving a false PRESENT, which the manual question is there to catch; and spelling one of these tokens is not proof the retrieval path filters on it, which is why both signatures matching escalates to MANUAL rather than passing.

bad.app/memory.py:
import json
import pathlib

STORE = pathlib.Path("memories.jsonl")


def add_memory(text, tags):
    """Append a fact. Nothing here can ever record that it stopped being true."""
    with STORE.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps({"text": text, "tags": tags}) + "\n")


def _load():
    return [json.loads(line) for line in STORE.read_text().splitlines()]


def recall(query, k=5):
    rows = _load()
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: similarity(query, r["text"]), reverse=True)
    return rows[:k]

good.app/memory.py:
import json
import pathlib

STORE = pathlib.Path("memories.jsonl")


def add_memory(text, tags, valid_until=None):
    rows = _load()
    rows.append({"id": len(rows), "text": text, "tags": tags,
                 "superseded_by": None, "valid_until": valid_until})
    _save(rows)
    return rows[-1]["id"]


def supersede(memory_id, replacement_id, at):
    """Record that a fact stopped being true, so retrieval can refuse it."""
    rows = _load()
    rows[memory_id]["superseded_by"] = replacement_id
    rows[memory_id]["valid_until"] = at
    _save(rows)


def _load():
    return [json.loads(line) for line in STORE.read_text().splitlines()]


def _save(rows):
    STORE.write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in rows) + "\n")


def recall(query, k=5, now=None):
    rows = [r for r in _load()
            if r["superseded_by"] is None
            and (r["valid_until"] is None or now is None or r["valid_until"] > now)]
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: similarity(query, r["text"]), reverse=True)
    return rows[:k]
